organism.overview: Latrodectus hasselti is a venomous spider that uses a web-associated bite to subdue prey and defend itself. Its venom contains neuroactive components associated with latrodectism.
naturalHistory: It builds irregular webs in sheltered locations.
The species is associated with human-modified habitats as well as natural environments.
Females are substantially larger than males.

deliveryMechanism.summary: Venom is delivered through the spider's fangs during a bite.
sequence: Spider contacts prey or a defensive target.
Venom is injected into the bite site.

habitats.name: Sheltered structures and dry habitat
habitats.summary: Webs are often built in sheltered spaces, including structures and ground debris.

ecologicalRoles.summary: Venom supports prey capture and defense.

summaryPoints: Redback spiders use venomous bites in predation and defense.
